applies_why: The judge text is grading a chain-versus-chain collision over Isaiah 7:14, so K-C governs whether it used a forbidden verse-level or stating-verse test.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse'—one reading treats the judge's wording/application split as an impermissible verse-level split, the other treats it as a chain-footing comparison; I adopt the latter.
why: The judge's stated reason compares what each side's chain answered and leaves the link underdetermined, rather than deciding from the absence of a contrary statement in any single verse.
